text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: P1 — Elevated 5xx observed for tenant HalcyonHealth on dedicated cluster dedicated-eu-west-2-7
incidents-bot: tenant=halcyon-prod, cluster=dedicated-eu-west-2-7, 5xx_rate=8.4% over 5m (baseline ~0.1%). dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/halcyon/overview
morgan: oncall here. paging infra + SRE. I'll start triage. Any early signals from nodes?
javier: checking nodes now. I see repeated CrashLoopBackOff and OOMKilled on a co-located tenant pod named batch-processor-omega. GPU mem at 98% on node-07. pulling logs.
javier: kubectl -n dedicated-halcyon get pods (snippet):
```
NAME                                     READY   STATUS      RESTARTS   AGE
halcyon-model-0                           2/2    Running     0          9d
halcyon-model-1                           2/2    Running     0          9d
batch-processor-omega                     0/1    OOMKilled   15         6h
proxy-gateway-0                            2/2    Running     0          2d
```
liz: Halcyon support: their API requests started failing around 02:20 UTC. They say traffic is steady but they have business-critical traffic right now.
ryan: FYI dedicated clusters are single-tenant "dedicated" by contract but we still colocate low-priority batch tenants on spare capacity. Looks like that noisy batch kicked off and is starving GPU memory.
incidents-bot: Event: autoscaler did not trigger due to reserved capacity flag on cluster; manual scale required.
morgan: mitigation options: A) throttle batch-processor-omega at the ingress, B) evict the offending pod(s), C) failover Halcyon to a lighter-quantized model, D) request immediate manual node add. I'll start with A+B in parallel.
javier: applying ingress throttle to tenant batch-processor (command): `redwoodctl tenants update --id batch-processor --qps 50`
javier: throttle accepted. also issuing eviction: `kubectl drain pod batch-processor-omega -n dedicated-halcyon --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
kube-bot: Pod batch-processor-omega evicted by javier at 1953456835.
morgan: creating a temporary routing rule to route Halcyon to redwood-lf-8bit (smaller mem footprint) with instant switch. dev-platform, please confirm routing change and canary.
dev-platform: applying routing change via control plane. snippet: 
```
POST /v1/routings/actions
{"tenant":"halcyon","action":"route","model":"redwood-lf-8bit","mode":"immediate","weight":100}
```
dev-platform: routing update applied. Halcyon now routed 100% -> redwood-lf-8bit.
javier: watching node metrics — GPU memory pressure dropping to ~60% after eviction and throttle. some model servers reconverging.
morgan: quick health check against Halcyon's endpoint: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://halcyon.prod.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'`
result: `200 0.23` (200 OK, 230ms). good sign.
incidents-bot: Alert update: 5xx rate down to 1.5% over 5m.
ryan: requested manual capacity bump to fleet: +2 GPU nodes to dedicated-eu-west-2-7, change ticket submitted (ETA ~20m).
tom: Halcyon ops confirmed they paused their batch-retries and are running a reduced QPS while we stabilize. they report internal retry rate spiked earlier which amplified errors.
morgan: action items while we wait for scale: 1) keep batch-processor throttled for 1h, 2) leave Halcyon on redwood-lf-8bit for 30-60m and monitor for regressions, 3) collect logs + trace spans for 02:10-03:00 UTC, 4) open INC-2026-458 and attach timeline. javier, can you gather runtime error lines?
javier: log snippet (model runtime):
```
[2026-03-15T02:27:02Z] ERROR decode_worker: OOM while decoding logits, triggered kv-cache flush. upstream handled error -> 502.
[stack: truncated]
```
morgan: file INC and escalate to oncall infra if scale stalls. also recommend follow-ups: tenant soft quotas, block sudden long-running batches without quota check, and a runtime guard to preemptively evict pods exceeding sustained memory threshold.
dev-platform: note — we pushed the routing change as an immediate switch rather than canary because of high impact. Recommend a post-incident review to evaluate safe canary flow for such scenarios.
incidents-bot: Severity: P1 -> mitigated (impact reduced). continuing watch for 60m.
javier: 10m after eviction metrics: 5m 5xx=0.45%, median latency=210ms, GPU mem avg=48%. cluster stability looks OK.
morgan: handing follow-up monitoring to javier. I'll be offline in ~30m. @javier please own INC-2026-458, timeline and RCA (root cause: noisy batch-processor without soft quota caused sustained GPU memory saturation -> OOMs -> 5xx for Halcyon; mitigations: ingress throttling, pod eviction, routing to low-memory model, manual capacity bump).
javier: taking it. I'll draft postmortem and include recommended runbook changes: auto-throttle policy, tenant batch-window detection, and a preemptive eviction threshold in scheduler.
ryan: infra to confirm node add completion and run a health sweep after scale.
morgan: closing active page. re-open if we see regression. thanks team. :thumbsup:
